Chan Master Lingsuan Weishen said: "The reason students of today have not yet escaped birth and death lies in what ailment?
It is simply that their 'thieving mind' has not died. Yet this is not their fault; it is the fault of the teachers.
It is like Emperor Gaozu of Han, who deceived and killed Han Xin. Although Xin was dead, was his mind truly dead? The students of antiquity spoke thus.
To escape birth and death below, where does the efficacy lie? It lies in the fact that the thieving mind has already died.
However, this is not something a student can achieve on their own; it is truly due to the teacher’s subtle and profound skill as a smith.

It is like Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty, who sat in the great hall and saw Hou Jing without shifting his voice or expression, yet the heart of Jing was already withered and drained of all remainder. What is said by various quarters is not so.
It is not beautiful. In short, it is like Zhao Mao’s painting of flowers; though the flowers are lifelike, they are not real flowers.
Tongrong said: "The talk of 'stealing the mind' is a common malady among students. From the subtle to the manifest, the process of arising and falling away exists within.
As for that which obstructs the chest, if it has not been removed, then when responding to events and interacting with things, one's radiance will not penetrate through."
It is so. Possessing right knowledge and vision, the spiritual friend unties their adhesions and removes their bonds; he extracts the nails and pulls out the wedges.
His own forging is indeed subtle and profound, ensuring that each and every one of them becomes like a lion or an elephant, like a tiger or a dragon.
This all depends on one’s own mastery. There was once such a person; try citing him and see.

At that time, Muzhou served as the First Seat (Dharma-seat leader) and asked, "How long have you been here, Senior Monk? The Master replied, "Three years. Muzhou said:

Cengcan asked, "Did you not ask? The Master said, "I did not ask. I do not know what to ask. Baizhang said, "Why do you not ask the Abbot, 'What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma'? The Master then went away. Before the sound of his question had even ceased, Baizhang struck him. When the Master came back down, Baizhang asked, "How was your inquiry? The Master said, "As soon as I made my inquiry—" "The sound of it," Baizhang interrupted. He struck him again. The Master bowed. Baizhang said, "You have just now asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma; why did you not understand? The Master bowed again. Baizhang said, "If you had understood at that time, you would not have been wandering in birth and death for so many years. The Master bowed once more. Baizhang said, "Go and wash your bowl. The Master went out. As he reached the door, Baizhang called out, "Heshang! The Master turned his head. Baizhang said, "This is precisely it. The Master attained enlightenment. At that moment, I suddenly realized that the myriad phenomena are all the Buddha-dharma. Nanquan said, "Mazu is a man of great capacity. Why did he strike you? Before he had finished speaking, the Abbot struck him. The Master said, “I do not understand. Baizhang said, “Just go and ask again. The Master asked once more, and Baizhang struck him again.

This happened three times; he asked three times and was struck three times. The Master said to Baizhang, “I have already received your encouragement to inquire about the Dharma, and I have repeatedly been granted your blows.
I regret that my own karmic obstacles prevent me from grasping the profound meaning. I shall now take my leave. Baizhang—
[The Master] said, "If you are going, you must first take leave of the Abbot before departing. The Master bowed and withdrew.

[Daowu] went first to Huangbo's place and said, "That monk who asked questions, though he is but a youth, is truly extraordinary. If he comes to take his leave, please receive him with skillful means."
In the future, he will become a great tree that provides shade for all people under heaven. The Master took his leave of Huangbo the following day.
Huangbo said, "There is no need for you to go elsewhere; simply go to Daoyu at Tancheng in Gaoyang to consult him; he will surely explain it to you.
When the Master arrived at Daoyu’s place, Daoyu asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "I have come from Huangbo. Daoyu asked, "What did Huangbo have to say?"
[The student] said, "I asked about the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma three times and was struck three times.
I do not know whether I have committed an offense or not. Yunju said, "Huangbo’s compassionate and earnest heart has brought you to utter exhaustion;
yet you come here again to ask whether you have committed an offense or not. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "So it is!"
"Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much. Yuyou grabbed him and said, "You little bed-wetting ghost!
Just now you were asking whether there was a fault or not; now you say Huangbo’s Buddha-dharma is not much. What principle have you seen? Speak quickly, speak quickly!
The Master struck Yuyou three times under the ribs. Yuyou pushed him away and said, "Your teacher..."
"Huangbo, it is none of my business," [the Master] said. The Teacher took his leave of Dayu and returned to Huangbo.

Upon seeing him, Huangbo asked, "This fellow comes and goes; when will he ever have an end to it? The Teacher replied, "It is only because of her grandmotherly concern. Then he performed the customary greetings.
He stood in attendance. Huangbo asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Yesterday, I received the Master’s compassionate instruction to go and consult Dayu.
Huangbo said, "What did Dayu say? The Master recounted their previous conversation. Huangbo said, "That old fellow Dayu is too talkative;
wait until he returns and I will give him a thorough beating. The Master said, "What need is there to wait? Strike him right now! He then followed after him.
Baizhang then slapped him. Huangbo said, "This madman has come here to stroke a tiger's whiskers. The Master then shouted.
Huangbo called to his attendant and said, "Lead this madman away to attend the hall."
Tongrong said: "Huangbo was thorough to the very bone and marrow for Linji;
it was only when he recognized [the truth] beneath Dayu’s words that he first realized the scale-weight was as hard as iron.

Nevertheless, while Linji’s realization of the Way was entirely due to Huangbo’s power, he also received assistance from Dayu. Furthermore, Dayu expanded upon it, saying: 'Your teacher Huangbo is not...'"
"Attend to my business. From this, we know that Dayu also possessed a mind of vast, open clarity;

he did not claim Linji as his own spiritual heir, but directly manifested the merit of Huangbo. Furthermore, it was because of Huangbo’s rigorous and pungent forging that Linji’s functional capacity suddenly emerged;
thus, Dayu did not take credit for it. Once Linji had attained enlightenment, he turned toward...
Dagyū’s three punches beneath the ribs directly clarify such a message;
Huangbo’s single slap transcends all cages and nets, like the Great Aca Sword whose blade-tip cannot be provoked.
Thus, the Linji school stands supreme under heaven—is this not because its source is deep and its stream long?
Chan Master Xinghua Cunjian of Weifeng was the head seat in the assembly of Sansheng.
He often said, "I have traveled throughout the south on my pilgrimage, yet I have never once encountered a single person with whom I could strike a chord regarding the Dharma."
The Three Sages heard of this and asked, "What kind of eye do you possess that you speak in such a manner? The Master then gave a shout. The Sages said, "It must be you who can do so.
Later, when Dajue heard this account being cited, he remarked, "How could the wind blow [this man] all the way into Dajue’s gate?
Subsequently, the Master became the head steward at Dajue’s monastery. One day, Dajue called out to him, "Head Steward, I—"
"I have heard you say that during your recent journey southward, you never once encountered a person who had truly grasped the Buddha-dharma with the tip of your staff.
On what basis do you speak thus? The Master then shouted; Huairang then struck him.

The Master shouted again. Jue struck him again. The next day, as the Master was passing by the Dharma Hall, Jue called out to the head of the monastery, "I have a direct doubt regarding those two shouts you gave yesterday.
The Master shouted again. Jue struck him again. The Master shouted once more. Jue struck him yet again.
The Master said, "I learned a 'phrase of host and guest' from my senior brother Sansheng, but it has been completely broken down by you, Senior Brother."
"You have failed! I wish to grant you, sir, a Dharma-gate of peace and happiness. Jue said, "You blind fellow!

You come here only to meet with defeat! He stripped his clothes and beat him severely. At these words, the Master realized the principle behind why his late teacher Linji had received blows from Huangbo.
Tongrong said: "Xinghua’s eyes were empty of the four seas; he was as if no one else existed. His pair of eyes had been struck down by Dajue.
At the point where it says 'Urgent as the Imperial Decree,' he met Linji face-to-face, and thus succeeded him.
Yesterday he gave two shouts, and today he gives two shouts—this is not considered excessive. Yet he says, 'I have learned this...'"
This dialogue between guest and host was entirely defeated by the elder brother; thus, many secrets were laid bare.
Had it not been for Dajue’s thorough application of the hammer and tongs, how could the principle of Linji receiving blows from Huangbo ever have been revealed?
When the Venerable Ding first visited Linji, he asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?

Linji descended from his meditation seat, seized him, and as the Master hesitated, Linji gave him a slap. The Master stood there lost in thought. A monk standing nearby said, "Venerable Ding, why do you not prostrate yourself?
Only then did the Master prostrate, whereupon he suddenly attained great enlightenment. Later, while traveling south, he encountered Yantou, Xuefeng, and Qingshan on the road.
The three men were at Yanhou’s place. Yanhou asked, “Where have you come from, Senior? The Master replied, “From Linji.

Yanhou said, “The Master is in good health, I trust. The Master said, “The Master has already passed away. Yanhou said, “We three specifically went there to pay our respects, but our merit was insufficient and we did not meet him.
I do not know what sayings or phrases the Master had while he was alive; I request that you, Senior, cite one or two instances for us.”

The Master then cited Linji’s ascent to the hall, where he said: "Upon this ball of red flesh there is a true person of no station who constantly enters and exits through the gates of the faces of you all.
Those of you who have not yet realized this—look! Look! At that time, a monk asked, "What is the true person of no station?
Linji stepped down from his meditation seat, grabbed him, and said, "Speak! Speak! As the monk hesitated, Linji pushed him away.
[Dongshan] said, "The 'true person of no station'—what kind of dried dung pellet is that? Yantou involuntarily stuck out his tongue.
Xuefeng said, "Linji is very much like a stealthy thief. Qingshan said, "Why not say that upon this ball of flesh there is no 'true person of no station'?
The Master then seized him and said, "The 'true person of no station' and the 'non-non-true person of no station' differ by no more than—"
"Too little! Speak quickly, speak quickly! Qinshan was thus captured; his face turned yellowish-green from distress, and he could not utter a word.
Yantou and Xuefeng said, "This newly ordained monk does not know good from evil; he has offended the Senior Monk. We hope you will show him compassion.
The Master said, "If it were not for these two old fellows, I would have beaten this bed-wetting ghost to death. This occurred while the Master was at Zhenfu.
After returning from his midday meal, he sat upon a bridge. He encountered three *zhu-zhu* (lecturers), one of whom asked, "What is the bottom of the deep river of Chan?
One must exhaust it to the very depths. The Master seized him and prepared to throw him over the bridge.
The other two lecturers stepped forward and pleaded, "Please do not take offense at our interruption; we beg you for your compassion. The Master said, "If it were not for these two lecturers..."
The Master said, "I shall simply lead him to the very bottom.
Tongrong said, "With one move from Linji and a single pressure from a bystander, I will cause this venerable monk to turn his body atop the flagpole, leaving no room for metaphysical understanding.
Thus, I captured Qinshan and cast out the Seat-Master, like a fish with a gill-slip of a foot. Not so.
It may be transgressed. Nevertheless, even though a sharp sword is keen, it does not slay one who is innocent.
What is this "one phrase of innocence"?
The practitioner Shoukuo traveled on pilgrimage to the assembly of Master Huayan at Qizhou. One day, Master Yan ascended the hall.
He said, "The great assembly today—if you are the descendants of Linji, Deshan, Gaoteng, Dayu, Niaoke, and Chuanzi—there is no need for 'how' or 'what.
Simply request to enter directly with a single blade, and Huayan will provide you with verification.
The Master came forward, bowed, and upon rising, he gave a shout. Huayan also shouted. The Master shouted again; Huayan also shouted. The Master rose from his bow and said:
The assembly watched this old man suffer a complete defeat. [Yanguan] let out another shout, turned his back to the assembly, and sternly descended from the seat to return to the abbot’s quarters.
At that time, Fengxue was serving as the *vinaya-dhara* (Rector). He went up to pay his respects, and Yanguan said, "Rector, you have come.
I cannot bear it that Shoukuo just now twisted and squeezed me; wait until the assembly has gathered, and I shall give him a beating."
Xue drove him out. Xue said, "It was too late to drive him out; it was the Master’s own fault for speaking thus. He is a descendant of Linji;
his true nature is simply this. Yan Fang calmed his anger. Xue went down and reported this to the Master.
The Master said, "For what reason did you try to persuade this fellow? Before I had even asked him, he already wanted to eat a blow of my staff. Now that my words have been carried out..."
"I do not strike. This remark of mine has already spread throughout the world. Xue said, "Even so, it has already pervaded the world.
Tongrong said, "Huayan had the head of a dragon but the tail of a snake; he could not cause Shoukuo to submit to his realization.
Had I been the mountain monk, when I saw him say, 'The assembly, behold this old fellow’s total defeat,' before the sound had even died away—"
He immediately struck him with his staff and drove him out. Not only were these two practitioners [of Zen] defeated, but it further demonstrated that the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*’s command was not in vain.
Yet, when he said to the *karmadāna*, "Wait until the assembly has gathered, then I shall give him a beating and drive him out," one could say he lacked courage in the moment.
To raise troops from within the ranks is yet another grave failure.
Zen Master Minde of Chengxin Monastery in Luzhou was at Xinghua when he encountered the following public address:
"If you are a veteran warrior, then please enter with a single blade directly; do not hesitate to ask 'how' or 'what'. The Master went out and prostrated; as soon as he rose, [he spoke].
Huihong shouted. Changhua also shouted. The Master shouted again. Changhua also shouted. The Master bowed and returned to the assembly.
Changhua said, "If it had been anyone else just now, thirty blows of the staff would have been due, and not even a single blow could have been spared. Why?
Because Minde understood a shout as not being used as a mere shout."
Tongrong said, "Minde is certainly a master; his style is self-evident.
Xinghua said, "It is because Minde understands that a single shout is not used as a single shout. Tell me, what is the meaning of this?
If you possess a single eye here, you will not fail to transcend the school and differ from the common view, becoming a true seedling of the lineage."
Chan Master Shanzhao of Taizi Monastery in Fenzhou was the son of the Yu family of Taiyuan.

Having shaved his head and received full ordination, he traveled with staff in hand, staying briefly wherever he went and responding to inquiries according to the capacity of those who approached him. He studied under seventy-one spiritual teachers before eventually arriving at Shoushan.
There, he asked, "What is the meaning behind Baizhang’s folding of his mat? Shoushan replied, "The dragon’s sleeve is swept aside, and the entire body is revealed."
The Master asked, "What is your understanding? Dongsan replied, "Where the Elephant King walks, there are no tracks for foxes. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Rising from his prostrations, he said, "The moon in the empty realm of the ten-thousand-year-old green pool—only after searching and stirring it again and again does one finally come to know it.
Someone asked, "What principle did you perceive that led you to such self-acceptance? The Master replied, "This is precisely where I let go of my body and life."
Tongrong said: "Shoushan’s response in this manner enabled Shanzhao to cut off heaven and earth, leaving no trace behind.
This was because the way of the teacher and disciple was in perfect accord; it was certainly not accidental. Observe how he studied under seventy-one spiritual friends (*kalyāṇamitra*);
his stripping away of the thicket and breaking through the film [of ignorance] was indeed manifold. Only when his intellect was exhausted and his efforts were spent could he truly accept himself."
You may not know this:
Chan Master Guisheng of Guangjiao Monastery in Ye County, Ruizhou, traveled to visit Shoushan.

One day, Shoushan held up a bamboo stick and asked, "If you call it a bamboo stick, you fall into the trap of 'contact'; if you do not call it a bamboo stick, you fall into the trap of 'aversion. What would you call it?"
Ma. The Master snatched it up and threw it on the ground. Shanshan said, "Blind! At these words, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
Tongrong said: "Last night a fire broke out; the flames were red both inside and out. Struck by it, everything was reduced to powder; even dull iron was turned into pus.
Now tell me, how far apart are the ways of [this Master] and those of Shoushan?
Chan Master Chizhuang Ciming Chu-yuan of Tanzhou heard of the renown of Fenyang and went to pay him a visit. Fenyang looked at him and silently took note of him as a vessel of potential.
For two years, however, he did not permit him to enter the inner sanctum; whenever Chu-yuan saw him, Fenyang would invariably scold him or disparage the various other schools.
Furthermore, when he did offer instruction, it was always of a mundane and vulgar nature. One night, Chu-yuan complained, saying, "Since arriving at this Dharma assembly, I have already..."
"Again, Xia, you have not received my instructions; you have only increased your worldly afflictions.

As the years and months pass in a blur, your own fundamental task remains unclarified, and you have lost the benefit of leaving the household life. Before he had finished speaking, Yang stared at him intently and scolded, "This is a bad teacher!

How dare you deceive me? In a rage, Yang raised his staff to drive him away. As the Master prepared to step forward to rescue him, Yang covered the Master's mouth. At that moment, the Master attained great enlightenment and said, "It is this!"
Knowing that Linji’s Way transcended ordinary sentiment, he served him for seven years before taking his leave. One day, the Master went to visit Chan Master Shen Ding Yin.

Master Ding was the foremost senior disciple of Mount Shou; his reputation was preeminent at the time, and among the *nàzǐ* (monks), none who were not of extraordinary refinement dared to enter his gate.
He had resided on the mountain for thirty years, and his disciples’ spirit overwhelmed all quarters. The Master’s hair was long and unkempt.

Jian was wearing tattered robes and spoke with a Chu accent. When he announced his arrival and stated that he was the Dharma-nephew [of Fenyang], the entire assembly burst into laughter. Zhao Ding sent a youth to ask, "Venerable sir, whose successor are you?
The Master looked up at the roof and said, "I saw Fenyang in person. Zhao Ding then emerged with his staff and looked back at him.
With a joyful expression, he asked, "Is there a 'Lion of the West River' in Fenzhou? The Master pointed behind him and shouted, "The house is collapsing!
The boy turned and fled; Huileng (Ding) looked back in startled alarm. The Master sat down on the ground, removed one shoe, and gazed at him.
Huileng was so dazed that he forgot his question and lost sight of where the Master had gone. The Master slowly adjusted his robes and continued walking, speaking as he went.
He said, "To see the person is not as good as hearing of their reputation," and then he departed. Cui Ding sent someone to pursue him, but it was to no avail.
Sighing, Ding remarked, "Fenzhou has such a son! From that time on, the Master’s fame grew weighty within the monastic community.
Tongrong said: "Fenyang’s character possessed the full power of a lightning bolt and the vast function of a revolving heavens.

He enabled Ciming to cast off the cage beneath his master's mechanism and emerge from the old nest; he recognized that Linji’s Way transcends ordinary sentiment and saw that Shending possessed the strategy of killing with bare hands.
Entering directly with a single blade, he deployed his own resources to pass beyond Fenyang’s gate."
Therefore, there were those with eyes that transcend the mundane realm—some who stood embracing a pillar while washing their feet, others who let go of the mooring rope to set sail;
how could one possibly fathom even a ten-thousandth part of their realization?
The layman Master Yang Yi, courtesy name Da-nian, was recognized as a "divine infant" when young; by his maturity, he bore a reputation for talent, yet...
He knew there was a Buddha. One day, while passing by his colleagues, he saw one of them reading the *Vajracchedikā Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*.
He laughed and reproached him, saying, "How can this possibly surpass the teachings of Confucius and Mencus? Why such excessive flattery? Because of this, the official read several fascicles himself.
At first, he was bewildered and possessed only a slight degree of reverence and faith. Later, he met with Lord Li Wei of the Hanlin Academy, who exhorted him to seek out and inquire [of masters].
When he subsequently served as Director of the Secretariat and was appointed to govern Ruzhou, he went first to visit Guanghui. Upon being received by Guanghui, the Lord immediately asked:
"A cloth drum is struck before the hall; who is the one who knows this music? Guanghui replied: "The wind that comes is deeply discerned. The Lord said: "If that is so, then the Zen guest..."

When they met, [Zhaozhou] merely snapped his fingers. Huì said, "A gentleman may enter. The official responded, "Yes, yes. Huì said, "The grass-robbers have been utterly defeated. During their conversation that night, Huì asked, "Inspector Mi, with whom have you ever discussed the Way? The official replied, "I once asked the Venerable Liang of Yunyan, 'What is it like when two great tigers bite each other? Liang said, 'A single unified form. I [asked him about this]. When the discussion reached the story of the *liang* (integrity) *jian-si* (abbot’s assistant) answering the dialogue of two tigers biting each other, Guanghui displayed the majestic power of a lion;

Among all those on this path, there are none who do not praise and submit to him. Generally speaking, this is largely due to his internal cultivation of latent virtue and his external response to the guidance and inspiration [of his masters].

Chan Master Cuiyan Zhenke of Hongzhou was a native of Fuzhou. He once studied under Ciming and subsequently spent the summer retreat at Jinkuan together with Attendant Shan.
Shan was a senior disciple of Ciming; Dao-wu Zhen and Yangqi Hui both held him in high esteem.
[The Master] subdued him. The Master, having personally encountered Ciming, prided himself on it, thinking there was no one in the world who could satisfy his mind.
[Zhao] Shan spoke well with him; knowing that he had not yet attained full penetration, he laughed at him. One day, while walking in the mountains, [Zhao] Shan launched a sharp verbal challenge.

Zhao Shan picked up a piece of tile or rubble, placed it upon a flat rock, and said, "If you can utter a turning word regarding this, I will grant that you have personally seen Ciming. The Master [tried to respond], but...

When Shanzhao looked at him from the right, he posed a question in response. Shanzhao rebuked him, saying, "Stop your thinking and cease your mental activity. Your emotional consciousness has not yet penetrated; when have you ever even dreamed of this?

The Master was filled with shame and trepidation, and immediately returned to Shishuang. When Ciming saw him coming, he rebuked him, saying, "A true practitioner on pilgrimage must know the proper timing.
What is so urgent that you have come here so early, before the summer retreat is over? The Master wept and said, "I was struck by my elder brother Shan’s poisonous heart."
Because he had ultimately obstructed people, Ming came to see the Master. Ming suddenly asked, "What is the great meaning of the Buddha-dharma?
The Master said, "Cloudless, yet clouds arise upon the ridge; the moon exists, yet it sets into the heart of the waves. Ming glared at him and shouted, "Your head is white and your teeth are gone!"
He still maintained this same view. "How can one escape birth and death? he asked. Master Ming was startled and sought instruction. Ming said, "Ask me.
The Master repeated the previous statement and questioned him. Ming shouted with a thunderous voice, "No clouds arise upon the mountain peaks;
the moon descends into the heart of the waves. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Tongrong said: "Attendant Shan is truly a man of bold spirit. Observing his true nature, he also possesses great brilliance.
However, because his mental ground was not yet thorough, he fell under the sway of the 'dead mechanism.
When he met Ciming again, [Ciming] stripped away Lake Tai for him and brought forth Lake Poyang. After that, no one could ever do anything with him; I knew he had emerged."
One must be a man of heroic spirit; only a lion’s cub can overcome such an adversary. Both masters possessed this quality.
Chan Master Wenyue of Yunfeng on Mount Nanyue was the son of the Xu family from Nanchang. He first went to Dayu, where he heard the following address to the assembly:
"Everyone gathers here to eat some vegetable broth. If you call it 'a ladle of broth,' you will enter hell as fast as a shooting arrow."
He then descended from his seat. The Master was greatly startled. That night he went to the Abbot’s quarters. Yunwu asked, "What do you seek by coming here?
The Master replied, "I seek the Dharma of the mind. Yunwu said, "The Wheel of the Dharma has not yet turned; the Wheel of Food must turn first. You are a young man with vigorous strength;
why do you not go out to beg for the sake of the assembly? I am too busy enduring hunger to have the leisure to explain Zen to you. The Master did not dare to disobey. Not long after—

Several times Jiuyuan moved to Cuiyan. After Master [Dongshan] finished submitting his memorial of resignation, he went to visit Cuiyan again. Dongshan asked for guidance regarding his future direction. Cuiyan said, "The Buddha-dharma has not yet reached you; it will only rot away. The snow is cold;
you should go beg for charcoal for the sake of the assembly. Dongshan accepted this command. When his duties were completed, he returned to the abbot’s quarters.
Cuiyan said, "The Hall Administration is lacking personnel; I shall trouble you with this task now. Dongshan accepted it but was unhappy, harboring resentment toward Cuiyan.
He did not leave his mind [on the matter] and sat upon the rear rack. Suddenly, the hoops of his wooden bucket came apart, and he fell from the rack.

At that moment, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and clearly perceived the point of Yankuan’s teaching. He hurriedly put on his *kāṣāya* robe and went up to the dormitory hall. Yankuan met him with a smile and said, "Venerable Karmadāna, rejoice!
Your great matter is now finished. The Master bowed twice and departed without uttering a single word. He served under him diligently for eight years.
Tongrong said: "Daiyu’s instruction for Master Yue was rigorous and without a single point of entry; yet even Master Yue found it difficult to receive the teaching.

Nevertheless, it was like spring returning to the great earth, where all phenomena are renewed. It was only when Master Yue was touched by the seasonal change that he first realized the spring breeze was filling his sleeves.
People today have a mixture of knowledge and views; they speak of principles while using Zen to guide others, and furthermore—"
To explain things as a mere matter of business—seeing that Daoyu acts in such a manner, one might likewise proceed to explain it for others, requiring people to rely upon and practice it.
Yet, through various indulgences and concessions, it is like a military raid or a rebellion that leaves people with no firm foundation.
How could they know that Daoyu dwells alone within the midst of the world?

The layman Li Duanyuan, a Regional Commander, had read Chan texts since his childhood while residing in the state academy. Although he later married and entered official service, he remained steadfast in his devotion to the ancestral Way.

Consequently, he built a dwelling resembling a *ārāma* (monastery) in the rear garden and invited Master Daguan to stay there, consulting him morning and evening to such an extent that he forgot both sleep and food.
One day, Daguan looked at the official and said, "Were it not for the power of manifesting [an emanation], how could you have reached this state? Alas..."
"What is this 'non-entrance'? The Duke asked, "Are heaven and hell existent or non-existent? I beg the Master to explain this clearly.
Guoan said, "The Buddhas speak of existence within non-existence; it is like seeing flowers in the sky with one's own eyes. Your Excellency seeks non-existence within existence."
To grasp at the moon in the water with one's hands—how laughable! Before one’s eyes, one sees a prison yet does not avoid it; beyond the mind, one hears of heaven and desires to be born there.

Yet one fails to realize that joy and fear reside within the mind, and that good and evil constitute the objective realm. If you, Great Minister, simply understand your own mind, naturally there will be no delusion.
The Minister asked, "How is the mind to be understood? Zhaozhou said, "Do not deliberate upon good or evil at all. The Minister said, "If one does not deliberate..."
Later, [Wang] Gong asked, "After death, where does the mind go? Guàn said, "Please first return to your residence, Great Minister.
Gong said, "As for when a person dies, where does the mind go? Guàn said, "If you do not know life, how can you know death? Gong said, "As for life, I already know it."
Guoan said, "From where does birth come? The official was at a loss for a response. Guoan rose, thrust his hand toward the official’s chest, and said, "It is right here.
What more do you intend to deliberate upon? The official said, "I have understood. Guoan asked, "How do you understand it?
The official said, "I only knew how to follow the path, unaware that I had missed the way. Guoan pushed him away and said, "A hundred-year dream—only today have I finally awakened. Once...
And he spoke in verse: "At thirty-eight years of age, I was muddled and knew nothing. When I finally attained knowledge, how was it different from my ignorance?
The vast waters of the Yangtze flow silently along the embankments; Master, you must return now, for the arrow-like waves surge eastward."
Tongrong said: "Daguang spent his days and nights forging and refining with Duanyuan, causing Duanyuan’s realization of the profound path to reach its peak and his karmic conditions to become mature.
At the point where he was hesitating, when pressed at the very corner of the knot, he immediately became 'the bowl slipping from the hand.'"

Only now do I realize that in one's haste to reach the destination, one fails to notice the path has been missed. It is like Sun Bin’s employment of military strategy, which led to the death of Pang Juan at Maling;
yet even Juan, his skills exhausted and his plans at an end, knew only to hasten toward his goal, unaware that he had lost his way.
Chan Master Shouduan of Baoyun in Shu Prefecture was the son of the Ge family of Hengyang. In his youth, he devoted himself to calligraphy and literature.

Upon reaching adulthood, he donned the monastic robes under Chan Master Yu of Chaling. He subsequently went to attend upon Yangqi, who asked him, "Who is the master from whom you received your precepts?

The Master replied, "The Venerable Yu of Chaling. Yangqi said, "I have heard that he had an awakening after falling while crossing a bridge; he composed a verse on it that was truly extraordinary. Can you recite it?"
"Do you remember? the Master recited: "I have a bright pearl; for a long time it has been locked away by the dust of worldly toil.

Today the dust is cleared and its light shines forth, illuminating the myriad peaks of the mountains and rivers. Daofu laughed and rose to leave. The Master was startled and could not sleep all night.
At dawn, he questioned him about it. It happened to be the end of the year, so Daofu said, "Did you see those who were performing the *ou-no* exorcism yesterday?"
Jian said, "Qiji. Qiji replied, "You fall short of him by a single tally. The Master was again startled and asked, "What is the meaning?
Qiji said, "He loves being laughed at; you fear being laughed at. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Tongrong said: "Yangqi was at Ciming’s assembly for many years serving as the *jian-si* (administrative head).

Without entering the formal hall rituals, he attained great enlightenment and expanded the Way of Linji. He received Baizun Wendeng, employing a mastery of seizing and releasing with extraordinary skill."

With mastery over killing and enlivening, they cause even Master Duan’s doubts to die instantly. Among the venerable ancestors of the past, there were none who did not possess the skillful means to capture dragons and seize tigers;
none who failed to realize the intent of the Westward Transmission, directly manifesting the wondrousness of the single-lineage transmission.
They are truly what is called "sons and grandsons who uphold the family estate" and "those who bring glory to the ancestral hall."
Zen Master Fayuan of Wuzu in Jinzhou went to visit Zen Master Yuanzhao Ben. Although he had exhausted his understanding of all ancient and modern kōans, there was only one case he did not understand:
a monk asked Xinghua, "What is it like when they come from the four directions and the eight points?
Xinghua said, "I strike the one in the middle. The monk bowed, and Xinghua said, "Yesterday I attended a village feast; on the way back, a sudden gale blew past."
A heavy rainstorm arose, but he managed to take shelter inside an ancient temple. He requested instruction from Linji Yixuan. Yixuan said, "This is a matter concerning the lineage of Linji;
you must ask his descendants to understand it. The Master then went to visit Chan Master Fushan Fayuan and asked about the previous dialogue.
Fayuan said, "I have a parable to tell you: you are just like someone from a village of three households."
A wood-seller at the market was standing with his carrying pole at a crossroads, asking people, "What matters is the Council of State discussing today?
The Master calculated silently to himself, "If this is so, there is still much that remains to be done.
One day, Yuan said to the Master, "I am old; I fear you will let your time pass in vain. You should go and rely upon Baoyun. This...
"Although Lao is a junior to me, I have not yet met him in person; however, having seen his verse on the story of Linji’s three blows, he must be one who can resolve my great matter.
The Master wept as he paid his respects and took his leave. Upon arriving at Baiyun, he raised the story of the monk asking Nanquan about the *maṇi* jewel and requested instruction.
Baiyun rebuked him, and the Master attained sudden enlightenment. He offered this verse of realization: Mountain...
"This former plot of idle land—I join my palms and earnestly ask the patriarch: how many times has it been sold only to be bought back again?
It is for the sake of pitying the pines and bamboos that draw in the pure wind. Yun received special certification (inka) and was ordered to oversee the milling operations.
Before long, Yun arrived and said to the Master, "There are several Zen practitioners who have come from Mount Lu; they all possess a point of realization. If you instruct them to speak..."
He spoke with a clear rationale; when the Master presented him with a causal inquiry, he understood it clearly as well, and when asked to offer a response, he was able to do so.
Yet, [the Master felt] he had not yet reached the ultimate point. The Master then harbored a great doubt and reflected to himself: "Since he has attained awakening, he can indeed speak of it."
"Clarification is also attained through clarification," he said. "How is it that I have still not reached it? He then investigated this for several days until, suddenly, he attained realization.
All that he had previously cherished was cast away at once. He ran to see Baiyun, who danced with hands and feet; the Master merely smiled.
Later, the Master said, "Because of this, I broke into a cold sweat all over my body, and I immediately came to understand 'a load of pure wind.'"
Tongrong said: "The ancients did not arrogantly assume the role of others; yet, they also did not allow the eyes of the various quarters to be obscured.
For instance, when Fushan Yuan pointed Fuzhou Wuzu Yan toward Baiyun Dan to visit him, it was truly an act of withdrawing oneself and yielding to another."

Among ten thousand, not one [would succeed]. Had Master Yan been sent there, they would have turned their hearts toward his Way; with a single rebuke, they would have been able to grasp the essential point.

This would not have been possible without Master Huiyuan’s recommendation. Although it was but a temporary journey on the road, Master Duan acted as a guide, ensuring they would surely reach their destination.
Thus, Master Yan was able to manifest the pure breeze of the "Lower Vehicle. Now tell me, what was the meaning?
What was the point?
Master Fuguo finally went to see the Fifth Patriarch and exhausted all his skillful means, yet the Patriarch would not grant him approval.

He then accused the Patriarch of trying to force others to change their ways, spoke insolent words, and departed in a fit of indignation. The Patriarch said, "Wait until you have received a hot beating."
While he was ill and being beaten, he finally reflected, "I am here. When the Master arrived at Jìnshān, he contracted a severe case of cold and was extremely distressed.

[The Master] tested him with what he had previously perceived, but nothing took effect. Recalling the words of the Fifth Patriarch, he made a vow to himself, saying, "When my illness subsides slightly, I shall immediately return to the Fifth Patriarch.

it is simply that the husband wishes to recognize the voice. The Commissioner responded, "Yes, yes. The Patriarch said, "But listen closely."
Just as the Master returned and stood in attendance, [Dongshan] asked, "I heard the Abbot recite a minor erotic poem; did the Provincial Inspector understand it?
Juefan said, "He only recognized the sound. Dongshan said, "It was only necessary for the lover to recognize the sound. Since he has already recognized the sound..."
"Why is it not so? The Patriarch asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
It is the cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master suddenly attained realization; he hurried out and saw a rooster fly onto the railing, spreading its wings and crowing.
He said to himself, "Is this not sound? He then tucked incense in his sleeve, entered the room, and presented what he had realized, offering this verse: "Golden duck..."
The incense has faded from the brocade curtains; amidst the sounds of pipes and songs, he is drunk and supported home.

This one episode of youthful elegance is known only to the beloved lady alone. The Patriarch said, "The great matter of the Buddhas and Patriarchs is not something that those of inferior capacity or weak roots can attain.
I rejoice with you. The Patriarch then addressed the elders of the mountain community, saying, "My attendant has realized Zen."
From this point on, he was promoted to the position of head monk.
Tongrong said, "The Fifth Patriarch acted in various ways for him; it is not that Foguo failed to see forms or hear sounds."
If one were to set aside the single phrase regarding "medicinal taboos," it would also be said that he does not look. Try to see for yourself with certainty.
This is the Great Wisdom (Dahui) Chan Master Zonggao of Mount Jing in Lin’an Prefecture.

When the Master arrived at Tianting [Tianning] Monastery, one day he heard Yuanwu ascend the hall and cite a monk’s question to Yunmen: “What is the place where all Buddhas emerge? Yunmen replied: “The East.”
"Ascending upon mountains and waters. If it were Tianning, it would not be so. Suppose someone were to ask, "What is the place where all Buddhas manifest?
he would simply say to him, "A fragrant breeze comes from the south; the halls and pavilions grow cool.
Under these words, the Master’s past and future suddenly severed. Although the movement of mental constructs did not arise, he nonetheless remained seated upon a ground of pure nakedness.
Wu said to him, "It was not easy for you to reach this state. It is a pity that you have died and cannot yet live again.
To harbor no doubt regarding words and phrases is the great illness. Have you not heard it said: 'Letting go at the edge of a precipice;
one who is willing to accept it for oneself revives after death; one cannot deceive the Master. You must believe that such a principle exists. He then had him reside in the Zemo Hall.
Acting as an attendant who did not manage affairs, he entered the master’s room daily with the Great Officer Wushi.

Every time Wushi raised the question, "The phrase with meaning and the phrase without meaning—like a vine leaning against a tree," the Master would just open his mouth, and Wushi would immediately say, "Not it, not it. This continued for half a year.
He then asked Wuxue, "I heard that when you were with the Fifth Patriarch at that time, you once asked this same question.
I do not know what the Fifth Patriarch said. Wuxue smiled but did not answer. The Master said, "At that time, you must have asked it before the assembly;
there would be no harm in saying it now. Wuxue, having no choice, said, "I asked: 'Is there a phrase or is there no phrase? It is like a vine leaning against a tree.'"
"What is the meaning? the Master asked. The Patriarch replied, "It cannot be traced; it cannot be painted. He asked again, "What does 'the tree falls and the vines wither' mean?
The Patriarch said, "They come along together. At that moment, the Master was suddenly relieved and said, "I understand!"
Dongshan Wuzhu then cited several cases of *nidāna* to interrogate him. The Master (Tongrong) responded without hesitation. Wuzhu said, "Now I know that I did not deceive you.
Tongrong replied, "When Daoyi first traveled among the various elder masters of the Dongshan school, he could not fully comprehend their teachings; it was only with Zhan..."
In the hall, after many years of forging and casting [his character], one day the Abbot said to Master Gao, "Upādhyāya Gao, you have comprehended the Chan of this place all at once.

If I were to teach you how to speak, you could speak; if I were to teach you how to compose *niangu*, *songgu*, *xiaocan*, or *pushe*, you could do them all. There is only one thing, however, that remains incomplete. Do you still..."
"Do you understand? He replied, "What matter is this? Zantang said, "You simply lack this one realization.
If you had not attained this realization, there would have been Zen for you when the Abbot spoke in the Dharma Hall; as soon as you left the Dharma Hall—"
[When] it is not conscious, there is nothing; when one is alert and deliberating, there is Chan. As soon as one falls asleep, the Chan disappears.
If this is the case, how can one confront birth and death? He replied, "This is precisely where I am in doubt.
Later, when Zhantang’s illness became critical, [Dongshan] asked him, "If you, Master, do not recover from this illness, whom should I rely upon to resolve this?"
"This is a great matter," he said. "There is a diligent fellow who does not even recognize the precepts.
If you see him, you will surely be able to accomplish this task. If you cannot find him, then go and practice; in a future life, come out to study Chan.
Following these instructions, the Master went to study under Yuanwu. At first, when the fragrant breeze blew from the south and the halls were cool, he immediately—
You sat there in majestic stillness, cutting off past, present, and future. Later, at that place where it cannot be depicted or painted, you suddenly recognized it clearly before your face.
Letting go from the precipice, you revived after being dead; this was truly the hammer and tongs of Yuanwu.

Chan Master Shaolong of Tiger Hill in Pingjiang Prefecture went to visit Yuanwu. One day, upon entering the inner quarters for instruction, Yuanwu asked: "When seeing the very act of seeing, that seeing is not [true] seeing;

even seeing is already detached from seeing, such that seeing cannot reach it. He then raised his fist and asked, "Do you see this? The Master replied, "I see. Yuanwu said, "This is adding a head on top of a head.
Upon hearing these words, the Master attained a sudden and profound realization. Yuanwu rebuked him, saying, "Seeing! (The Master was struck silent).
"What is the principle here? The Master said, "The dense bamboo does not hinder the flowing water from passing through.

Wuzu accepted this. Tongke remarked, "Wuzu acted for the sake of Shao Long; from a ground of thorough realization, he drew forth the 'blow-off hair sword' (chuimaojian), severing everything down to the finest detail.
Master Long was thus left with no place to seek refuge. Yet, it was like a cricket running through fire while carrying the moon in its mouth."
Chan Master Fozhi Duanyu of Yuyang Mountain in Qingyuan Prefecture went to see Yuanwu late in his life at Zhongfu.
One day, Yuanwu asked, "Who knew that the Eye of the True Dharma would be extinguished upon this blind donkey? Is it extinguished right now, or not?
The Master replied, "I ask the Master to please close his mouth. Yuanwu said, "This is still not beyond the realm of ordinary sentiment. As the Master was about to speak—
"Correct. Wuzu struck him. The Master immediately cast off what he had been stuck on.
Tongrong said, "Wuzu’s hook and awl are swift and sharp. When he uses the hook, it moves the sinews and bones;
when he uses the awl, it teaches the blood to flow. This results in the very life-force of Buddha-wisdom being non-existent. Now tell me, how will you pass your days? He gave a shout.

Chan Master Yunbian of Nanfeng in Pingjiang Prefecture later went to attend Yuanwu. Upon entering the inner chamber for instruction, as soon as he stepped through the door, Yuanwu said, "Look beneath your feet.
The Master struck a pillar once. Yuanwu said, "Why do you not speak a single word that hits the mark?
The Master replied, "If the teacher nods his head, the disciple wags his tail. Yuanwu said, "Try wagging your tail for me. The Master performed a somersault.
As he stepped out, Wuzu laughed loudly.
Tongrong said, "Cloud-Discernment may indeed wag its tail, but if it encounters a lotus root hole, its tail will certainly not be able to pass through."
Chan Master Huiyuan of Lingyin Monastery in Lin’an City: When Yuanwu returned to lead Zhaojue Temple, the Master went there and heard Yuanwu’s general discourse (*pushe*).
Yuanwu cited the karmic cause and condition concerning Layman Pang asking Mazu, “Do you not take all dharmas as your companion?

At that moment, the Master attained sudden enlightenment and collapsed among the assembly. The assembly helped him up, whereupon the Master said, “I have awakened from my dream. Later, during the night *xiao-can* (small private instruction), the Master...

He came forward and asked, "It is pure, naked, empty, and without a single thing; it is bare bones, destitute, and without a single coin. My house is shattered and my family is lost; I beg the Master for relief.
Wu said, "The seven treasures and eight jewels are all seized at once. The Master said, "Calamity does not enter the door of a prudent household.
Wu said, "The pivot does not leave its place; you have fallen into a sea of poison. As soon as these words were spoken, the Master let out a shout. Wu—
Holding his staff, he struck the meditation seat and asked, "Have you eaten the blow yet? The Master also shouted. Wuzhuo shouted twice in succession. The Master then bowed.
From this point on, his spiritual acuity became sharp and piercing, such that nothing could obstruct or contradict it.
Tongrong said, "Huiyuan was under the guidance of Yuanwu; he was able to investigate with utmost diligence. Thus, from the moment he entered the gate, he attained complete mastery.
Although Yuanwu employed all manner of methods to ensnare him, in the end, he could not turn him back."
Chan Master Ch’e-an of Zhaojue in Chengdu Prefecture relied upon Yuanwu at Jingshan. He informed [Yuanwu] of his insights, but Yuanwu did not approve.

When Yuanwu was summoned by imperial decree to reside at Yunju, the Master followed him there. Although he attained a degree of conviction, he remained suspicious because a "thorn in his chest" had not yet been removed.
It happened that Yuanwu asked the assembly of practitioners, "When the time of birth-and-death arrives, what then? A monk replied:
Xiangtaizi Xiaheshang asked the Master next, "How do you understand this? The Master replied, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated.
Wuzu said, "If someone were to ask you this, how would you respond? As the Master was about to answer, Wuzu pressed him with the words, "The grass-thief has been utterly defeated!
At that moment, the Master attained thorough realization. Wuzu struck him with his fist, and the Master clapped his hands and laughed loudly. Wuzu asked, "What have you seen?"

It was exactly so. The Master said, "The poisonous fist has not yet been requited; it shall not be forgotten for eternal kalpas. Wuzhuo returned to Zhaojue and was appointed as the head of the assembly.
As Wuzhuo was about to pass away, he entrusted the succession of the seat to the Master.
Tongrong said: "Since Ch'e-an had already attained thorough realization, when Yuanwu struck him with a fist again, it should not be understood as a test;
it should not be understood as a blow to the back of the head; nor should it be understood as a probing rod. Tell me, how was it?"

"Eh! Chan Master Ren of the Rantang Hall at Zhongtianzhu in Lin’an Prefecture, after receiving full ordination, traveled back and forth to the Tripitaka Translation Institute, where he thoroughly investigated the sutras and śāstras;
yet, he remained particularly unconvinced by the School of the Patriarchs (Zongmen). At that time, Yuanwu was residing at Tianning. [Ling...]

He went to pay his respects at dawn. Baizhang Huaiwu was then leading the assembly into the inner room for meditation. Upon seeing him, the Master was filled with reverence and resolve; he stepped forward boldly.

Huaiwu said, "To explain the meaning based on the scriptures is to be at enmity with the Buddhas of the three ages; to depart from a single word of the scriptures is to speak like a demon. Speak quickly! Speak quickly!
As the Master prepared to respond, Huaiwu struck him across the mouth with his staff, causing a tooth to fall out. At that moment, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Tongrong said: "Youtang has come and gone among the translation bureaus, thoroughly investigating the sutras and śāstras until he has become a rotting winter melon.
Upon meeting Yuanwu’s single squeeze, it will shatter into pieces. However, the stem within the melon must not be touched;
if it is touched, disaster will ensue."
One day, while Chan Master Yuan Jue of Mount Xiang’er in Meizhou was reciting the Lotus Sūtra, he reached the passage:

"Furthermore, one does not even know what is the fire and what is the house. At that moment, he attained sudden enlightenment. When he finished his retreat and returned home for a visit, Chan Master Xingjian nodded in approval.

Yuanwu was again granted imperial permission to reside at Yunju. When the Master arrived there, he reported what he had attained to Yuanwu. Yuanwu rebuked him, saying, "This is fundamentally a pure land;
why are you defecating here? At these words, the Master's doubts were suddenly resolved.
Tongrong said: "Yuanjue, at the 'Fire House' chapter, stripped off his outer robes; under Yuanwu’s words, he removed his inner shirt.
Although I, this mountain monk, have rendered such a judgment, regarding Yuanjue’s own part, there is still one phrase that has not been spoken.
Now tell me, what is that one phrase?"
The Marquis Zhao Lingjin, courtesy name Biaozhi, styled Chao’ran Jushi, went with Grand Secretary Wang Zao, Councilor Li Bing, and Vice Minister Zeng Kai to Mount Jing to visit Dahui.
When Dahui heard of their arrival, he ordered the drum to be struck to summon them into his room.
The Marquis joyfully approached him carrying incense in his sleeve. Dahui said, "Regarding the story of Zhaozhou washing the alms bowl, what does the Layman say?"
"How do you understand this? The Master said, "What bowl are you looking for? He then shook out his sleeves and went out.

Huì hurried after him, grabbed hold of him, and said, "The ancients attained enlightenment right here; why do you not attain it? As the Master was about to respond, Huì struck him and said, "What bowl are you looking for?
The Master said, "Only when I return this to the old man will it be right."
Tongrong said: "Chao ran shines in his cutting and tailoring; Da hui secretly pierces the needle. Chao ran’s cutting and tailoring have a graceful air to behold;
Da hui’s secret piercing of the needle gathers and breaks through the thread. When examined critically, both men deserve thirty blows of the staff."
Furthermore, tell me: where does the fault lie?

When Zen Master Wenshu Xindao of Changde Prefecture heard Zen Master Fojian’s night discourse citing Zhaozhou’s “Cypress Tree” koan, he arrived at the point where Jue Tiezui said, “The former master did not say such words;
do not slander the former master. Because of this, [Xindao] was greatly...

He was filled with doubt. After a long period of intense mental exertion, one night he suddenly attained enlightenment. He immediately hurried to the master’s quarters, intending to recount what he had realized.
As soon as Xuedou Jue saw him approaching, he closed the door. The Master said, "Master, do not deceive me. Jue replied, "The ten directions have no walls;
why do you not enter through the door? The Master punched a hole in the paper window. Jue immediately opened the door, grabbed him, and said, "Speak! Speak! The Master—
He held the mirror in his hands, blew upon it with his mouth, and departed. He then presented this verse: "Zhaozhou has the 'Pine Tree' koan;
Zen practitioners have transmitted it throughout the world. Most merely pluck at the leaves and search for the branches, Unable to understand it directly at its very source.
Master Jue says there is no such thing— This is truly like reviling one’s face with foul words. If a Zen person possesses..."
Tongfangyan was fond of discerning the true from the false within this matter. Fodian Shen admired him and would always praise his countenance.
Later, Shen invited him to share his seat.
Tongfangyan said, "Fodian Shen closes the door, yet Shen can discern the wind coming from afar; Mind-Path (Xindao) breaks through the window, yet he cannot grasp it."
It was precisely because he recognized the "pine tree" that his eyebrows and beard fell out.
Chan Master Shouxun Fodeng of Heshan in Anji County was the son of the Shi family of that prefecture. He went to consult with Chan Master Guangjian Ying, but there was no accord;
he then traveled to Taiping, where he joined the assembly to seek instruction, yet he made no progress at all. Thereupon, he sealed his own coffin.
He said, "If I do not thoroughly penetrate this life, I vow never to unroll this [mat]. Thereupon, he sat by day and stood by night as if mourning for his deceased parents.
After more than seven weeks had passed, Master Fojian ascended the hall and said, "The myriad phenomena of the universe are all sealed by the One Dharma.
Upon hearing this, the Master attained sudden enlightenment. He went to see Fojian, who said, "What a pity! A single bright pearl has been lost amidst this madness."
Han Shide then questioned him, saying, "Lingyun said, 'Since the moment I first saw the peach blossoms, until this very day, I have had no further doubts.
What is it about him that he has no doubts? The Master said, "Do not say that Lingyun had no doubts;
even now, if you search for a single point of doubt, it is utterly unobtainable. Jian said, "Xuansha said, 'How perfectly true! How perfectly true! Daring..."
"Brother Bao has not yet reached the ultimate point. Where is it that he has not reached it? The Master said, "I know deeply that you, Venerable Sir, are earnest in your compassionate concern.
[Bao] acknowledged this. Rising from his prostrations, the Master presented this verse: "All day long I gaze at the sky without raising my head;
Only when the peach blossoms are in full bloom do I lift my gaze. Even if you possess a net that covers the heavens, Once you have penetrated the secure barrier, you may simply rest."
Jian instructed him to protect and uphold [the teachings]. That evening, he spoke to the assembly with a stern voice, saying, "The Senior Monk Xun is sleeping soundly.
When Yuanwu heard this, he suspected it was not so and said, "I must put him to the test before I can accept it. He then sent someone to summon him.

While traveling together in the mountains, they happened upon a mountain pond. Huineng pushed the Master into the water and immediately asked, "What was it like before Niutou saw the Fourth Patriarch?
The Master replied, "The pond is deep and the fish gather. Huineng asked, "What was it like after he saw him? The Master replied: "The pond is shallow and the fish scatter."
"A tree high up catches the wind. Wuzhuo asked, "What is it like when one has seen and when one has not yet seen? The Master said, "Stretching out one's legs while they are still tucked away.
Wuzhuo praised him greatly.
Tongrong said, "Among those who practice Chan meditation, there is none who cannot attain thorough awakening like Old Xun.
Nevertheless, he reached the stage of non-doubt through the seal of the Buddha-eye master Foguan. Therefore, when Yuanwu subjected him to testing, it was extremely arduous;
yet he never changed countenance."
Chan Master Shigui of Zhuanan at Longxiang Temple in Wenzhou was the son of the Shi family of Chengdu. Initially, he relied upon Zongya of Daci Temple;
his mind became intoxicated by the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* for more than five autumns. He then traveled south to pay homage to various venerable masters, finally ascending the Dragon Gate (Longmen).
There, he presented to Foyan what he had attained during his ordinary life. Foyan said, "Your understanding of the mind is already ultimate; you simply lack the effort to open your eyes."

Furthermore, he was subsequently appointed to the position of Hall Attendant (*tangsi*). One day, while standing in attendance, [Zhaozhou] asked, "What is it like when all dependencies are transcended?
Guanyin replied, "It is just like when you strike the gavel in the Sangha Hall. The Master was at a loss. That evening, Guanyin went to the Hall Attendant’s quarters;
the Master brought up the previous conversation. Guanyin said, "That was just idle talk. At these words, the Master attained great enlightenment.
Tongrong said: "If Shi Gui had attained enlightenment upon the very first word of the Buddha-eye, he would certainly have become a master of the school who does not stray.
It was improper for him to achieve great awakening under the influence of idle words and phrases;
he cannot avoid being like one who abandons a boat or throws himself into fire. If you encounter a person with clear eyes, feel free to present this to them."
Chan Master Mingbian of the Main Hall at Daochang Monastery in Anji Prefecture heard a monk cite a poem by Fuyan that elucidates the story of King Kaniṣka of Kaśmīra beheading the Venerable Siṃha:
"By the Yangzi River, willows bloom in spring; Willow catkins sadden those crossing the river.
The sound of a few pipes from the Qiang people lingers as evening falls on the palace grounds; You head toward the Xiang River, while I go toward Qin."
The Master had an inner realization in silence; he immediately went to Longmen to seek entry into the room.

Foyan asked, "I allow that you have understood the causes and conditions regarding the records of the ancestral masters from of old. Suddenly, Foyan raised his fist and said, "Why is this called a fist?
The Master was about to respond when Foyan struck him in the mouth, saying, "Do not apply intellectual reasoning! Thereupon, the Master's conceptual knowledge and views were instantly cast away.
Tongrong said: "Why is this called a fist? Face-to-face presentation is as swift as a flying arrow.
If a patch-robed monk understands the principle of the arrow leaving the string, he will clearly discern and penetrate Vimalakīrti."
Chan Master Miaoguang Haichan Jiaozhong of Quanzhou visited Chan Master Yuanwu at Yunju. He subsequently studied under Huangbo Xiang and Gaoshan Wu;
their exchanges and words were all in accord. Due to the outbreak of bandits in the Huai and Chu regions, he returned to visit Foxin.
It happened that Dahui was staying at Guangyin, so he went to follow him there. Dahui said to him, "Try [to explain] what you have attained while with Foxin."
To illustrate one or two cases for you to examine: The Master cited the public case of Fuxin’s ascent to the hall regarding Puhua, saying, "Fuxin would not have done it this way.
When none come in such a manner, what then? He struck him across the spine, leaving him to manifest his body throughout the entire world.
Hui asked, "What is your opinion on this? The Master said, "I do not approve of the footnote he added at the end. Hui said, "This..."
This was precisely taking illness as the Dharma. The Master resolutely refused to believe it. Huì said, "You simply try to contemplate it. The Master thought this was not so.
After ten days had passed, he recalled Zen Master Haiyin Xin’s remark: "The sound of thunder is vast and great."

There were no raindrops at all. For the first time, he was without obstruction. He hurried to inform Huì, who cited the words of Langya and Xuansha regarding the one who "sees the Way" yet remains unpenetrated.
Huì interrogated him; after the Master had replied, Huì said with a smile, "Although you have advanced one step, you have merely failed to find your place.
It is like a person cutting down a tree: if one strike is dealt beneath the root, the life-force is severed. You, however, are still on the branches."
"Chop! Can that sever the life-root? Nowadays, those who discourse on Chan in all directions are for the most part like this in their views;

what benefit does this bring to the matter? Of the direct lineage of Yangqi, there are only three or four people. The Master departed in indignation. On another day, Huì asked him, "Do you still have doubts?
The Master said, "There is nothing to be doubted. Huì said, "It is just as when the ancients met one another."
"Even before he has opened his mouth, one already knows whether he is empty or substantial; or upon hearing his words, one immediately recognizes their depth or shallowness. How is this principle so?
The Master was struck with awe and broke into a sweat, not knowing where to turn. Huì commanded him to investigate the "phrase with meaning" and the "phrase without meaning.

Later, when Huì visited Yunmen’s hermitage, the Master accompanied him as an attendant. One day, he asked: "I have reached this point, yet I cannot attain thorough penetration. Where does my illness lie?"
Huì said, "Your illness is most chronic; even the physicians of the world fold their hands in helplessness. Why?
Because others die and cannot be revived, whereas you have already been revived and have never died. To reach the ground of great peace and happiness, you must undergo one more death.
The Master’s state of doubt deepened further. Later, when he entered the room, Huì asked, "The rice gruel has been eaten, and the bowl has been washed. Now, cast it away!"
Regarding the "Taboos on Medicine": "The Way-Master, bring me a single phrase. The Master said, "Torn asunder. Huizhen struck him with a thunderous shout and said, "You have spoken of Chan again!
At that, the Master attained great enlightenment. Huizhen beat the drum and addressed the assembly, saying: "Turtle hair makes one laugh heartily;

With a single blow, the locks of ten thousand leagues are opened. Joy and fulfillment for a lifetime come this very day; Who says I was deceived by a thousand miles? The Master [was thus enlightened].
He also presented it in verse, saying: A single pressure brings forth the roar of a thunderbolt striking the target; It startles the Mount Sumeru that conceals the Northern Dipper.
The vast waves surge, flooding the heavens; The nostrils are plucked away and the mouth is lost.
Tongrong said: "Miguang previously had his words and insights in perfect accord with four elderly masters;
yet, when it came to Dahui’s words, he could not depart. This was because his 'thieving mind' had not yet died out and his attachment to appearances still remained. Dahui’s skillful means were high:
he caused him to strip away the skin and flesh, and finally applied the hook deeply within the marrow."

Zhuì: "He was able to hold his alms bowl directly toward the ground; because he had attained liberation through his realization, Mahāmati could not help but rejoice, and thus spoke this verse specifically to express his seal of approval."
*The Ancestral Hall’s Record of the Tongs and Hammers*, Volume Upper;
*The Ancestral Hall’s Record of the Tongs and Hammers*, Volume Lower.
Compiled and authored by the Ming dynasty ancestral successor, the Śramaṇa Feiyin Tongrong.
The layman Xia Chunhui and Gong Shilong compared the records of Chan Master Lan’an Dingxu of Xichan Monastery in Fuzhou. [Dingxu] had traveled extensively to study under renowned masters;

finding no difference in the flavor of the Dharma, he returned to his native village and built a hermitage on the summit of Jiangfeng Peak, where he did not descend for three years. Miaoxi built an hermitage at Yangyu; the Master...
Fuyou Miguang sent a letter to the Master, saying: "The master's skillful means differ from those of other quarters. How about coming for a brief visit? The Master did not reply.
Miguang then used a ruse to invite the Master for a meal, and the Master went to attend. It happened that Miaoxi was conducting the *ru-shi* (entering the room) session for his disciples;
the Master joined him to express his appreciation. Miaoxi raised the case of a monk asking Mazu, "What is the Buddha? to which Mazu replied:
"This very mind is Buddha. What do you say to this? The Master gave a response. Miaoxi rebuked him, saying, "With such a level of understanding, how dare you presume to act as a teacher to others?
He then beat the drum for a public sermon, exposing the points upon which the Master had relied throughout his life as being merely matters of personal attachment and effort.
He categorized [the Master's teaching] as a heterodox interpretation. The Master’s tears drenched his chin; he did not dare look up at him and thought silently to himself:

"Since that which I have realized has been rejected, can the essential meaning of the 'untransmitted doctrine' from the West be limited to this alone? He then returned his heart to the ranks of the disciples.
One day, Xì asked, "When one does not let [the mind] go out within, nor allow it to enter from without—what is it like at such a time?
As the Master was about to open his mouth, Xì took up his bamboo staff and struck him three times across the spine.
At this, the Master attained great enlightenment and cried out in a stern voice, "The Master has already given too much! Xì struck him once more, and the Master bowed. Xì smiled and said, "Today..."
"Only now do you know that I have not deceived you. He then sealed [the teaching] with a verse, saying: "The eye of Mahesvara stands upright at the crown of the head;
behind the elbow hangs askew the talisman that snatches life. Blinding the eyes and discarding the talisman—Zhaozhou hangs his gourd upon the eastern wall.
Thereupon, his fame resounded throughout the monastic community.
Tongrong said: "Dahui’s tongs and bellows rise far above all quarters; therefore, those who follow him are numerous, and those who attain the Dharma are likewise abundant.
At the Yangyu Hermitage in Changle, in barely fifty days, he brought eleven people to awakening, and Lan’an was among their number.
Furthermore, although Lan’an has already emerged as a teacher for others, he still [criticizes]..."
Those points upon which he had long cherished and relied as his own strength, he now cast aside as erroneous interpretations, leaving others with a desolate air.
When pressed at the throat, one was forced to open one's eyes at the crown of the head. Who but Mahamati could have accomplished this?
Chan Master Fozhao Deguang of Yuyang in Qingyuan Prefecture was the son of the Peng family from Linjiang Commandery.

At the age when he resolved to study the Way, he received the tonsure under Chan Master Ji of Guishua Temple on Mount Dongshan in his native prefecture. One day, upon entering the master’s room for instruction, Ji asked:
"It is not mind, not Buddha, and not a thing. What is it? The Master was at a loss and became filled with doubt; he did not sleep all night.
The following day, he went to the abbot’s quarters to seek further instruction, saying, "Yesterday, I received the Master’s question: since it is neither mind..."
"It is neither Buddha, nor is it an object. Ultimately, what is it? I hope the Venerable Master will compassionately point this out to me.
Ji-zhen Wei let out a shout and said, "This śrāmaṇera wants me to provide a commentary for you! He seized his staff and struck him across the back, driving him away.
At that moment, the Master attained realization. Later, he visited Yue-an Guo, Ying-an Hua, and Bai-zhang Zhen.

He ultimately could not bring himself to accept it. Shortly thereafter, when Dahui was presiding over the Yuyang Monastery, the elite talents from across the four seas gathered there like scales of fish, and the Master was among them.
In Dahui’s room, Dahui questioned the Master: "If you call this a bamboo whisk, you commit the fault of 'contact'; if you do not call it a bamboo whisk, you commit the fault of 'aversion.

You may not utter a word, nor may you remain silent. As the Master was about to respond, Dahui struck him with his staff. At that moment, the Master attained a sudden and great enlightenment. From then on...
What he had attained crumbled like falling masonry and melted away like ice.

Tongrong said, "Fozhao had an awakening under Master Ji; he also visited various great elders, yet he ultimately would not acknowledge it himself, because the lotus root was severed but the fibers remained unbroken.
Dahui, however, was like seawater flowing upstream against the current. As for Jiang... [text fragment]
The lake has overturned.
Chan Master Tanyi of Yuyuan in Fuzhou had long relied upon Yuanwu and considered himself free from doubt.

At the beginning of the Shaoxing era, he went forth to reside at Xiangyun in Xinghua, where his Dharma assembly was quite flourishing. When Dahui entered Min, he realized that Tanyi’s realization had not yet reached its ultimate depth, and thus...

The order arrived for the Master to come. The Master delayed. Hui gave a small-scale *can* (private instruction), severely rebuking him, and furthermore posted a public notice to the fourfold assembly.

The Master had no choice but to break the summer retreat to visit him. Hui questioned him thoroughly regarding his realization. Afterward, he said, "With such a view as yours, how dare you claim to be the successor of Elder Yuanwu?
The Master withdrew from the monastery to stay with him. One day, during a private session, Hui asked, "I want someone who does not..."
A master of Chan was appointed as National Teacher. The Master said, "I am going to become the National Teacher. Huì shouted him out.
Not long after, Huì said to him, "Xiangyan’s place of awakening does not lie in the striking of the bamboo; Jūzhi’s attainment does not lie on the tip of his finger.
Thereupon, the Master attained sudden enlightenment.
Tongrong said: "The family tradition of Linji is to drive the plowman’s ox and snatch the hungry man’s food.
Dahui exposed Dingxu’s lifelong cherishing of views, categorizing them as heterodox interpretations;

he severely rebuked the lack of clarity in Tan Yi’s insights, causing others who were ready for the occasion to let go and turn themselves around in a single stroke. Truly, he can be called a man of such caliber."
The three men from Mount San were attendants who had long served Dahuì. They had once silently investigated the "Bamboo Cudgel" koan but had made no progress.
One day, after leaving the inner quarters, they requested instruction. Dahuì said, "You are people from Fuzhou. I shall give you a metaphor:
it is like taking a fine-grade lychee and peeling away the skin and shell all at once, then placing it directly into your mouth with your hand."
"It is simply that you do not know how to swallow it. The Master could not help but laugh and said, "If the Abbot swallows it, then it will be a matter of regret."
Later, Huì asked the Master, "Regarding the lychee you swallowed the other day, it was simply that you did not know its flavor.
The Master said, "If one were to know its flavor, one would see even more troubling matters."
Tongrong said: "Dahui’s saying 'to speak is also to attain' is correct; to understand closely is also to understand intimately.
But as for the phrase 'wild geese falling on the flat sand,' how would you say it?"

The lay practitioner Wu Weiming, a Provincial Commissioner for the Investigation of Crime, whose courtesy name was Yuanshao, had long studied under Chan Master Zhenxie Liao and attained the realization of "self-enjoyment" as his ultimate goal.
Later, he visited Dahui at the Yangyu Hermitage and joined the assembly for the private interview (入室).

When Dahui raised the koan regarding the absence of Buddha-nature to question him, Wu attempted to respond; however, Dahui struck him with his bamboo staff. Wu was left speechless and subsequently remained there to engage in intensive inquiry and practice.
One day, Huì said to him, "You need not display your clever skills; you must simply 'crack' with a sudden burst and 'sever' with a sudden snap, only then can you confront birth and death.
If you merely display your clever skills, what end will there ever be? He then took his leave. While traveling along the Yanping River, he suddenly attained enlightenment.
He wrote several verses in succession and sent them to Huì, all concerning the questions he had previously asked in the master's room. One of them read: "It is not the mind."
It is not a thing; it is not a thing. His entire body is a single set of golden chain-bones. Zhaozhou personally saw Old Nanquan, who could say, "Zhengzhou produces radishes.
Hui then spoke a verse to certify this, saying: "His entire body is a single set of golden chain-bones, Fit to serve as a model for gods and humans.
If you wish to recognize Linji’s little servant boy, He is none other than the man from those days."
"Pickpocket!
Tongrong said. "Although Weiming has awakened to the fact that he possesses a set of golden-locked bones, this is not in doubt;
yet if he encounters one who 'beats the bone to extract the marrow,' he will surely be forced to surrender. However, to be able to act as a 'white-handed thief' is [something else]."
Linji was his fellow practitioner.
The Inner Secretary, Layman Zeng Kai, whose style name was Tianyou, had long studied under Yuanwu and had spent many days coming and going at Dahui’s gate.
In the *Xinwei* year of the Shaoxing era, when Fohai was appointed to Guangxiao Temple in Sangu, the Master and Layman Chaoran—
Lord Zhao visited him and asked, "What is a good spiritual friend (kalyāṇamitra)? Haichang replied, "The lanterns, the pillars, the cats, and the dogs.
The Lord said, "Why is it that when you praise them they rejoice, and when you disparage them they suffer? Haichang replied, "Minister, have you ever met a good spiritual friend?
The Lord said, "I have been seeking and questioning for thirty years; why do you say I have not seen one? Haichang said, "Toward..."
[Zhaozhou] saw [Haihui] at the place of joy; he saw him at the place of affliction. Zhaozhou prepared to deliberate; Haihui made a sound like a thunderous roar and shouted.
Zhaozhou prepared to respond; Haihui said, "The one who opens his mouth is not [it]. Zhaozhou was clearly enlightened. Haihui called out, "Attendant, where have you gone?
